306	### 4.3 Algorithm at the reservation gate (manager thread)
307	
308	Inserted after the existing downgrade branch, i.e. once `reservation`, `freed` (0 when there
309	was no downgrade executor) and `reservation_info` are final (between `:273` and `:277`):
310	
311	```cpp
312	auto* cur_local = dynamic_cast<gpu_pipeline_task_local_state*>(gpu_task->local_state());
313	bool const retried = cur_local && cur_local->original_task_id.has_value();
314	if (retried && _policy.max_futile_attempts > 0) {
315	  auto const grant = reservation->size();
316	  auto const floor = reservation_info.retry_reservation_floor;
317	  bool const grant_below_floor = grant < floor;
318	  bool const nothing_freed     = freed == 0;
319	  bool const no_completion     = _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == cur_local->progress_epoch_at_reschedule;
320	  bool const nothing_running   = _progress->inflight_first_attempts.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;
321	  // Second, independent trigger: the space cannot give more than everything it has.
322	  bool const whole_space_granted = space_max > 0 && grant >= space_max;
323	  cur_local->gate_flagged_futile = (grant_below_floor && nothing_freed && no_completion && nothing_running) || whole_space_granted;
324	  if (cur_local->gate_flagged_futile) {
325	    SIRIUS_LOG_DEBUG("... task {} (original {}) attempt {} flagged futile at the gate: grant {} < floor {}, downgrade freed {}, "
326	                     "usage {}/{} bytes, resident outside live reservations ~{} bytes, completions since reschedule 0, first attempts in flight 0", ...);
327	  }
328	}
329	```
330	
331	Nothing else changes at the gate: the task is still dispatched with its partial reservation.
332	Two hygiene additions on the same thread, both no-ops today for non-error runs:
333	
334	- Before `make_reservation` (`:203`): `if (_completion_handler && _completion_handler->has_error()) { /* drop task; continue */ }`.
335	  After an error, the manager must not block another ~40 ms per queued retry in
336	  `make_reservation` while `drain_after_error` waits to join it (`task_executor.cpp:97-99`).
337	- Before dispatch: if the task is a first attempt (`!retried`) increment
338	  `inflight_first_attempts`; the dispatched lambda owns an RAII guard that decrements on every
339	  exit path (success, reschedule, exception). The guard is created inside the lambda so a
340	  dispatch that never runs cannot leak a count.
341	
342	### 4.4 Algorithm in the reschedule path (worker thread)
343	
344	Replaces `:339-364` (constants -> policy) and extends the local-state copy at `:385-395`:
345	
346	```cpp
347	auto const max_retries = _policy.max_retries;
348	if (next_retry_count > max_retries) { /* unchanged: exceeded-retries error */ }
349	
350	// Futility: a gate visit flagged this attempt and it OOMed anyway; and still nobody progressed.
351	uint32_t futile_attempts = 0;
352	if (cur_local && cur_local->gate_flagged_futile &&
353	    _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == cur_local->progress_epoch_at_reschedule) {
354	  futile_attempts = cur_local->futile_attempts + 1;
355	}
356	if (_policy.max_futile_attempts > 0 && futile_attempts >= _policy.max_futile_attempts) {
357	  _futile_aborts.fetch_add(1);
358	  auto const message = format_futility_error(*gpu_task, *cur_local, ex, futile_attempts, next_retry_count - 1, max_retries);   // section 4.5
359	  SIRIUS_LOG_ERROR("GPU Pipeline Executor: {}", message);
360	  if (_completion_handler) { _completion_handler->report_error(std::make_exception_ptr(std::runtime_error(message))); }
361	  return;   // identical exit shape to the exceeded-retries path: report_error only, drain_after_error does the rest
362	}
363	_oom_reschedules.fetch_add(1);
364	... existing WARN at :366 ...
365	new_local_state->retry_count = next_retry_count; new_local_state->original_task_id = orig_task_id;
366	if (cur_local) { new_local_state->inherit_retry_state(*cur_local); }      // floor + pin, as today
367	new_local_state->futile_attempts              = futile_attempts;          // 0 if progress happened or the gate did not flag
368	new_local_state->progress_epoch_at_reschedule = _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
369	std::this_thread::sleep_for(_policy.backoff);
370	```
371	
372	Ordering argument (why the epoch is read in three places): it is snapshotted when the retry is
373	created, compared at the gate, compared again at the OOM. A completion anywhere in that window
374	resets `futile_attempts` to 0. A completion is the only event that can turn a full pool into a
375	grant, other than a downgrade (covered by `freed`) or the CN engine thread freeing parked
376	repositories (cannot happen during a run: one fragment at a time, `engine.rs:278-280`, and the
377	engine's single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_`, report B1).
378	
379	### 4.5 The error message
380	
381	Built from what the executor can see; everything is a plain number, no attribution the
382	executor cannot back:
383	
384	```
385	GPU pipeline task cannot make progress and is failing the query: original task 2567 (pipeline 0,
386	OOM at operator GPU_SCAN (index 0)) OOMed on 3 attempts (2 consecutive futile) of at most 100
387	retries; memory space GPU:0 usage 107,374,182,400 / 107,374,182,400 bytes, ~94.1 GB resident
388	outside live task reservations (parked or idle batches this task cannot evict); last attempt:
389	reservation 3,318,948,864 bytes (retry floor 6,637,897,728), allocation request 748,875,880
390	bytes, peak 3,376,381,184; downgrade sweep freed 0 bytes (no spillable batches; DISK tier not
391	configured); no task completed since the previous attempt.
392	```

394	Sources: usage/limit = `_memory_space->get_max_memory() - get_available_memory()` and
395	`get_max_memory()` (`memory_space.hpp:113-116`); "resident outside live reservations" =

397	allocations, `reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`; **inference**: this equals idle
398	data plus running tasks' overflow, close to but not exactly the parked bytes, so the text says
399	"parked or idle"); grant/floor from the local state's `reservation_size_info`; request/peak from
400	`oom_details`; `freed` carried on the local state from the gate; DISK from
401	`_downgrade_executor->has_disk_tier()`. The CN adds its own outer frame today ("fragment
402	instance ... failed: failed to execute fragment: ..."); fix 2 (bookkeeping) is the right place to
403	append the CN's exact parked-slot totals if wanted.

431	
432	- ERROR line with the full message (4.5) once per abort; DEBUG line per flagged gate visit
433	  (bounded by `max_futile_attempts + 1` per original task); the existing per-retry WARN stays.
434	- `executor_metrics{tasks_executed, oom_reschedules, futile_aborts}` via `get_metrics()`;

438	- Quent: unchanged FSM (`quent::task::TaskHandle`, `sirius_pipeline_itask.hpp:110`; the
439	  finalizing event carries only `success`). The aborted attempt is finalized by the task
440	  destructor exactly like the exceeded-retries path today. The per-operator Computing sums shrink
441	  by construction (2543 -> ~75 GPU_SCAN executions for q05), which is itself the measurable
442	  signal in `quent_bp.py` output.

444	### 4.8 Cancellation and concurrency
445	
446	- **First error wins.** Both new exits use `report_error` (first-call-wins). Concurrent workers
447	  in the reschedule path see `has_error()` at `:314` and return without re-queueing; the manager
448	  loop's new `has_error()` check stops feeding retries. `drain_after_error` then interrupts the
449	  pool and queue and joins the manager (`task_executor.cpp:78-114`). Measured drain today: 71 ms
450	  (engine-cn0.log:61725-61735); the new check can only shorten it.
451	- **Downgrade cancellation.** `request_downgrade(...).get()` throws when the downgrade executor
452	  shuts down (`cancel_pending_requests`, `downgrade_executor.cpp:481-490`); the existing catch
453	  at `:239-244` breaks out of the loop; untouched.
454	- **Counter integrity.** `inflight_first_attempts` is incremented on the manager thread before
455	  dispatch and decremented by an RAII guard inside the lambda; exceptions, reschedules and
456	  successes all pass through the guard's destructor. `completed_epoch` is incremented where
457	  `_tasks_executed` is today (`:310`). Both are relaxed/acquire atomics on a struct owned by the
458	  `task_scheduler`, which outlives its executors (it destroys them in `~task_scheduler`).
459	- **Multi-GPU.** The struct is shared by every executor the scheduler creates
460	  (`task_scheduler.cpp:117-124`, GPU and HOST tiers), so a first attempt running on GPU 1 (the
461	  build task holding a batch in the contention case) suppresses the flag for a retry on GPU 0.
462	  HOST-tier executors' completions also count as progress; that only makes the check more
463	  conservative (delays an abort by at most one round), never less safe.
464	- **No engine-side cancel exists** (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476` is a stub; `sirius_ffi.cpp`
465	  has no abort entry). The design does not depend on one; when one lands it will use the same
466	  `report_error` and inherit the same drain.
467	- **Watchdog.** Untouched. Note for later hardening (out of scope): excluding rescheduled tasks
468	  from `query_progress_fingerprint` (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`) would let the 60 s CN watchdog
469	  catch storms this predicate misses.
470	
471	### 4.9 The contention case, explicitly
472	
473	`MAX_RETRIES` was raised 10 -> 100 for SF100 Q11, `cache=table_gpu`, `num_gpus=2`: the build
474	batch is held in `processing` on one GPU while a probe task on the other GPU needs it; each
475	convert-release cycle is O(100 ms) (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:339-347`). That OOM comes out of
476	`prepare_for_processing` (`gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:639-665`, `sirius_physical_operator.cpp:83-115`,
477	`batch_lock_utils.hpp:67-186`). Two independent reasons the flag cannot be set there:
478	
479	1. The pool is not at its limit (the problem is a lock, not bytes), so `make_reservation` grants
480	   in full and the partial-reservation branch that computes `freed`/`grant_below_floor` is not
481	   entered. The retry floor is only ever compared with a partial grant.
482	2. Even if the pool were coincidentally full, the task that holds the batch is a first attempt in
483	   flight on the other executor -> `nothing_running == false`, and when it finishes
484	   `completed_epoch` advances -> `no_completion == false`.
485	
486	So that case keeps exactly today's budget: up to 100 retries x (50 ms + gate). The same holds
487	for `cuda_launch_reschedule_exception` (`d42ff3e4`): it is not an OOM, the gate is normally
488	satisfied, the flag is never set.

496	Round period is unchanged (1.007 s: 25 tasks x ~40 ms of manager time; the storm's pacing is

502	| +2.66 .. +3.59 s | round 2 gate visits: retried, `freed==0`, grant 3.3 GB < floor 5.8 GB, no first attempt in flight (the last one OOMed at +2.62), epoch unchanged for all tasks rescheduled after the late success -> flagged. They OOM (~40 ms later) -> `futile_attempts=1`. |

636	## 9. Risks and failure modes
637	
638	| # | failure mode | when it can happen | consequence | mitigation in the design |
639	|---|---|---|---|---|
640	| 1 | False abort of a query that would have recovered | memory released by an actor the four signals cannot see | query fails ~2 s after its OOMs with a clear message instead of possibly succeeding | signals cover task completion (epoch), running tasks (in-flight), spill (`freed`); the only remaining actor is a concurrent query on another context in the same process, which the single-flight lifecycle excludes today; `max_futile_attempts` tunable, 0 disables; confirmed by an actual OOM, never by the gate alone |
641	| 2 | Fail-fast never fires | a first attempt is perpetually in flight elsewhere, or completions keep trickling | falls back to exactly today's 100-retry behaviour | acceptable by construction; the hard cap is still there |
642	| 3 | Race between gate flag and OOM | a completion lands after the gate check | the OOM would count as futile | epoch re-checked in the reschedule path; any change resets the count to 0; default N=2 absorbs one more |
643	| 4 | Counter leak in `inflight_first_attempts` | an exit path without the guard | flag suppressed forever (fail-fast disabled) or never suppressed (false aborts) | RAII guard inside the lambda; component test 1 asserts the counter is 0 after drain |
644	| 5 | Tests relying on `MAX_RETRIES = 100` timing | `test_oom_reschedule.cpp:445-560` asserts `oom_count >= 10` | none: that task's floor is 0, so the flag cannot set | keep the test; optionally speed it up with `max_retries` |
645	| 6 | Wrong attribution in the error text | "resident outside live reservations" is usage minus reservations, not parked bytes | operator misreads 94 GB as "parked" when 104 GB was parked and ~10 GB was in-flight overflow | wording "parked or idle batches this task cannot evict"; fix 2 can append the CN's exact parked totals |
646	| 7 | HOST-tier executors count as progress | HOST executors exist in `task_scheduler` | abort delayed by <= one round | acceptable; documented |
647	| 8 | Post-error manager blocked in `make_reservation` | queued retries after the first error | `drain_and_wait` join waits for a release (today 71 ms, releases are frequent) | new `has_error()` early-out before the gate blocks |
648	| 9 | Config schema change under `sirius.executor.pipeline` | existing YAML | none: old keys parse unchanged; `reject_unknown` still guards typos | parser test with a pre-change YAML |
649	| 10 | Whole-space trigger fires on a pessimistic estimate | request clamped to `space_max` on an empty space, task OOMs anyway | abort after N attempts | if the whole space was reserved and the task still OOMed, it needs more than the space; nothing in the engine can help |
650	
651	Determinism: the decision depends on timing only through "did anyone finish in between", which
652	is exactly the property that decides whether a retry can help; the outcome for a stuck task is
653	the same on every run (fail), the exact attempt count may vary by one. No wrong result can be
654	produced: the change only converts a slow failure into a fast one.

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).
16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.
20. DONE q15 determinism A/B on 1 CN (6 runs each): SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1 -> rows per run ['0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0'] (ms ['10331', '5161', '5182', '5002', '4876', '4809']); gate off -> rows ['0', '0', '1', '0', '0', '0'] (ms ['10576', '4795', '4847', '4799', '4661', '4788']). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).
21. CORRECTION to fact 6: the A/B in fact 20 REFUTES the simple hypothesis that the SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS gate alone explains q15's empty runs: with the canonical sort ON, 4 of 6 runs still return 0 rows (gate off: 5 of 6). The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. Standalone Sirius keeps DECIMAL and returns the row every time. Treat this as a correctness finding about equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; verify from cn1-canon-q15/ and cn1-nocanon-q15/ logs (declared cardinalities of streams 18/22 per run) and the translator's decimal->FP64 lowering (#1236, cast_to_fp64 in expr_translator.rs).

3:#### B1 (confirmed). Receiver-first rendezvous plus one fragment at a time turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation
5:**Source (verified).** `engine.rs:278-280`: `// One request at a time until the handle (and its sender) is dropped` `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()`; `run_fragment_inner` (engine.rs:486-720) does declare -> `build()` -> `relay_from` each parked sender -> `run()` -> park (engine.rs:697-716). `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from` throws unless the source fragment has run. `local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready` returns a receiver only when every expected sender is complete. The remote path is also park-then-export (`EngineRequest::ExportNext`, engine.rs:91-95). Inside the engine, `Fragment::build()` opens a `StandaloneQueryScope` that takes the single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_` (`sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596`) until `run()` finishes, so two fragments cannot be in flight on one context even if the CN asked (source skeptic; this makes "run sender and receiver concurrently" engine work, not CN work).
7:**Measured, q05 timeline.** All 11 `exec_plan_fragment` RPCs arrived 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cn1/cluster.log 4142-4202). Fragments ran strictly sequentially: nation 6 ms, region 9 ms, then the lineitem sender 5774 started 13:03:43.434 with `allocated=2304 bytes` (engine-cn0.log:49203, an empty pool) and parked 39 batches x 2.668 GB = 104.06 GB by +1.315 s (Quent data_batch Stationary events: 26.7 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s); first OOM at +1.361 s (engine-cn0.log:49221 `requested 748875880 bytes ... global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864`). The supplier/customer/orders fragments started only after the failure at 13:05:24.632+ (cluster.log 6072-6305); the receiver of streams 7 and 9 never started (Quent shows 7 of 11 fragments). Receiver 5775 later ran in 73 ms and its output sat parked for 184.5 s until q08's failure wipe (cn1-quent.txt wall=184.502 s, Comp=0.128 s).
9:**Measured, passing queries show the same shape under the cap.** cn1 q07.r0: all 7 senders finished before the join fragment started (cluster.log 6807-7005); 59.47 GB of lineitem plus 18.38 GB of orders were parked (79.1 GB, 74% of the pool) with dwell up to 2.76 s. cn4 q07.r1: every `fragment run finished` precedes its first `transmitted batches via nixl`. Per-fragment run sums vs span (MFS-4): cn1 q02.r1 13 fragments sum 977 ms, span 1067 ms, gaps 90 ms (8%); cn4 q02.r1 cn0 sum 748 ms, span 1081 ms, gaps 333 ms (31%), the largest before receivers waiting for the other CNs' senders. The 4-slot executor idles during the many 1-task fragments (cn1 q02.r1: 133 tasks, Comp 2.9 s in a 1.06 s span = 2.7 of 4 slots busy).
15:#### B2 (confirmed, mechanism sharpened). Parked batches are invisible to the downgrade sweep, so every OOM cycle frees 0 bytes although a 160 GiB HOST tier is configured
19:**Source (verified).** `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`: `// Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup so sender output outlives this fragment.` `_output_repos[id] = std::make_shared<cucascade::shared_data_repository>()` (and `_input_repos` likewise). The only registration path into a per-query manager is `repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:68-71 add_new_repository` (inter-pipeline ports). `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232` TIER 1 iterates `_data_repo_registry.get_all()` managers only; `:294-300` TIER 2 the pipeline task queue (queued GPU_SCAN tasks hold no input batches). The warning at `:357-363` fires whenever no DISK tier exists and the request is unsatisfied, regardless of whether any candidate existed. `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:1062-1066 output_row_count` throws on a non-GPU-resident parked batch (the CN swallows it with `.ok()` and plans blind, engine.rs:564, 582-585); `:822-825 export_packed` throws too, which would fail the 4-CN path on a spilled batch.
25:**Proposed.** Register the streaming sink's output repositories and the receiver's input repositories with a process-level registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, including the running fragment's own sink (otherwise q05/q08/q09 still die). Make `Fragment::output_row_count` read a row count from host metadata and `export_packed` accept HOST-tier batches (the local relay already upgrades HOST -> GPU in `lock_or_prepare_batch`). Correct the warning to distinguish "no convertible candidates" from "no disk tier". Note the newest-first fairness policy at `downgrade_executor.cpp:204-216`; the candidate that matters here is the newest fragment's own output. Confidence high on the mechanism, medium that spill is worth doing before P1/B1.
27:#### B3 (confirmed). The reschedule loop has no feasibility check: 179 stuck scan tasks x 100 retries x 50 ms, re-reading the split each time, while nothing can free memory
29:**Source (verified).** `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348 static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;` (comment: bumped from 10 for cross-GPU batch-lock contention), `:409 sleep_for(50ms)`, termination only by count (`:349-364`) or `_completion_handler->has_error()` (`:314`); `:263` proceeds with a partial reservation after 0 bytes freed. Each retry resumes at operator index 0 and re-runs `materialize_table` for the same split (`sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:530-533, 592-593`). No knob: `exec/config.hpp` has no retry field.
33:| query | stuck tasks | reschedules | first OOM (from client start) | last reschedule | wall to die (s) |
42:Offsets are from the client start in `cn1/runs/runs.csv` (q05 13:03:43.185); B1's "+1.361 s" for q05 is the same first OOM (13:03:44.795) measured from the lineitem sender's start (13:03:43.434). Every original task reaches exactly retry 100; the retry chain of q05 task 2567 is byte-identical on all 101 attempts (requested 748,875,880 B, peak 3,376,381,184 B; the retry floor raised the request from 5.80 to 6.64 GB while the grant stayed at 3.08-3.32 GB = cap minus parked bytes). Quent q05 fragment 5774: `GPU_SCAN n=2543 Computing sum 229.5 s` (about half of it is the 50 ms sleep, which Quent counts inside Computing), `Queued 2228.6 s`, `Reserving 99.9 s`, for 40 useful batches that took 1.3 s. The storm is paced by the single manager thread blocking in `make_reservation` (Reserving sum equals the retry window: q05 99.9 s of 101.2), not by the sleeps. Exactly one successful task finalised after the first OOM in each of the six windows. The six failures consumed 774.9 s of the 910.3 s 1-CN sweep (85%). Log volume: 89,580 of 152,097 engine-log lines are the five per-retry lines. `SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS` cannot detect the storm because each reschedule creates and destroys a task, advancing the watchdog fingerprint (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`).
44:**Proposed.** At the reservation gate (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263`) abort the query when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry_reservation_floor > reservation->size()` (all three are local there), or in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and `global usage == usage_limit` and no successful completion happened since this task's previous attempt (`_tasks_executed` at `:310` is success-only). Keep the 100-retry budget for the contention case, which arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the reservation gate. Message the engine can emit: "104 GB parked by this fragment's sink, 3.1 GB grantable < 6.6 GB floor, downgrade freed 0 bytes". Effect: each failure dies in ~3 s (q18 ~10 s because its own senders run first). Confidence high; this is a robustness finding, no wrong result is produced.
46:#### B4 (disputed: mechanism confirmed, causal claim refuted). Fragments of a failed query keep running and park output nobody consumes; the leak is 0-38 GB per failure but decided no pass/fail here
48:**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:449-476 cancel_plan_fragment` only calls `results.cancel()`; its log line reads `acknowledging cancel_plan_fragment (best-effort: no engine-side abort yet)` (:468) and the docstring says teardown "is a separate work item". `engine.rs:291-316` drops parked outputs only when `run_fragment` returns `Err`, and then wipes every slot process-wide. `ResultStore.query_failures` (result_store.rs:98) is recorded but never consulted on the sender path. A translator failure before the run (q16) drops the `LocalParked` slots without `drop_parked`.
50:**Measured** (engine-cn0.log `[gpu_pool] allocated` at fragment boundaries, agent-notes/refute-oom5/headroom.txt `base@start`): after q05 4.69 GB carried through q06/q07; after q08 8.83 GB into q09; after q09 31.56 GB through q10..q16 (seven queries); +6.6 GB from q16's parked partsupp scan -> 38.16 GB at q17's start; after q17 4.0 GB into q18; after q18 0; after q21 36.64 GB into q22 (q22 cold 4110 ms vs 943 warm). cluster.log shows the dead query's queued senders starting after `fragment run failed` (q05: 5773, 5777, 5776, 5775 at 13:05:24.632+, the first 0.25 ms before the FE's first cancel ack). Engine-thread time stolen from the next query: q17 -> q18 6.42 s, q21 -> q22 ~3.35 s, q08 -> q09 1.04 s.
52:**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. Every passing query that ran under a leak passed with `oom_resched=0` (q06/q07 under 4.69 GB, q10-q15 under 31.6-38.2 GB, q22 under 36.6 GB). No pass/fail in this campaign was decided by the leak. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).
54:**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.
56:#### B5 (confirmed, proposals corrected). Shuffle drains are serialised after the fragment finishes, and 84-88% of each drain is `export_packed` on the engine thread at ~63 GB/s
62:**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.
64:**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.
66:#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure
76:#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan
80:**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).
84:#### Disputed backpressure finding
86:**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.
88:#### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)
94:## 4. What to do first
100:| 1 | Fail fast in the OOM reschedule loop when the downgrade freed 0 bytes, usage == limit and the retry floor exceeds the grantable reservation (B3) | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263` (reservation gate) or `:330-420` (reschedule path) | the six failures die in ~3 s instead of 54-232 s (measured: 775 s of the 910 s sweep); the error names the real cause | keep the 100-retry budget for the cross-GPU contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory`, not the gate); needs `freed`/`global_usage` plumbed into the reschedule path if implemented there | high |
101:| 2 | Per-query parked-output bookkeeping: drop only the failed query's slots, skip its pending `Run`s, drop slots on cancel and on pre-run translation failure (B4) | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:291-316, ~626-643`; `compute_node_service.rs:449-476, 864-905, 1325-1400`; `local_exchange.rs` | removes the 0-38 GB leaks (measured) and 0.4-6.4 s of stolen engine time per failure; restores order-independence of results | Err-time bookkeeping is required (cancel arrives after the next sender started) | high |
103:| 4 | Make the six queries runnable on 1 CN: either (a) same-node fragment fusion before translation, or (b) parked repositories visible to the downgrade sweep + HOST-tier `output_row_count`/`export_packed` (P1, B1, B2) | (a) `compute_node_service.rs process_fragment` / `local_exchange.rs register_receiver` at the `TPlan` level; (b) `src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`, `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825, 1062-1066` | (a) reproduces the standalone plan that passes all six at 2.7-6.4 s; (b) five of six would plausibly pass slowly (q09 marginal at ~253 GB vs 279 GB GPU+HOST) | (a) substantial; 1-CN only; q21 also needs #5; (b) medium effort; spill throughput unknown | medium |
110:| 11 | Cold-start scan reservation: use the decoded column-buffer estimate instead of 8x (C3); fix the q07-type DF dependency (P5 FWJ-3) | `src/op/scan/sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:648-668`; `src/planner/sirius_plan_comparison_join.cpp:646-664` | first 4 requests drop from ~20 GB to ~7 GB, removing the 47-178 ms gate blocks at 1 CN and enabling more pipeline slots; ~0.25-0.3 s in q07's join fragment | verify no OOM reschedules appear | high (estimate), medium (DF) |

| `report_error(exception)` | Atomically sets exception on promise (first caller wins) |
| `get_awaitable()` | Returns the future for blocking |
| `is_completed()` / `has_error()` | Atomic status checks |

All methods are idempotent: the GPU epilogue and terminal pipeline may signal the same completion,
and only the first call takes effect.

## Reschedule Handling (OOM and CUDA launch failures)

**File:** `src/include/pipeline/oom_reschedule_exception.hpp`

Retryable execution failures are modeled as a small exception hierarchy: `task_reschedule_exception` is the base, with two subclasses —

- `oom_reschedule_exception` — a GPU operator ran out of memory. Carries `intermediate_data` (partial results computed so far) and `_resume_operator_index` (which operator to resume from).
- `cuda_launch_reschedule_exception` — a transient CUDA kernel-launch failure. `gpu_pipeline_task` translates retryable `thrust::system_error` codes (`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` / `cudaErrorInvalidValue`, seen from concurrent PDL launches in `cudf::hash_partition`) into this exception rather than failing the query.

The GPU executor catches the **base** `task_reschedule_exception` and:

1. Checks if the completion handler already has an error (skip if so)
2. Increments `retry_count` (max 100 retries, `MAX_RETRIES`)
3. Logs the retry attempt
4. Marks the original task as rescheduled (skips pipeline completion tracking)
5. Transitions intermediate data from idle to `task_created` state
6. Creates a new rescheduled task via `create_rescheduled_task()` virtual factory
7. Sleeps 50ms for backoff
8. Reschedules the new task back through the manager loop

If max retries are exceeded, the error propagates and terminates the query.

## Error Handling and Draining

**File:** `src/pipeline/task_scheduler.cpp`

`drain_after_error()` performs a multi-stage clean shutdown:

1. **Stop task creator thread pool** — prevents new tasks from being created
---EXECFLOW---
2. **Send task request** — signals the pipeline executor that it can accept work
3. **Pop task** — blocks until a `gpu_pipeline_task` is available
4. **Reserve memory** — acquires GPU memory reservation from `memory_space`
5. **Dispatch to worker thread** — on the thread pool with a CUDA stream:
   - Lock input batches and convert to GPU if needed (`lock_or_prepare_batch`)
   - `compute_task()`: iterate **all** operators in the pipeline (source through sink), calling `execute()` on each
   - `publish_output()`: call the sink's `sink()` method to push results to downstream ports
   - On OOM: catch `oom_reschedule_exception`, retry up to 10 times with 5ms backoff
   - On success: check if query is complete (RESULT_COLLECTOR sink + pipeline finished)
   - If not complete: schedule downstream consumers via `task_creator->schedule()`
   - If complete: `completion_handler->mark_completed()`

The GPU epilogue usually signals completion. A query-terminal pipeline also signals from
`sirius_pipeline::update_pipeline_status()`, covering finish transitions driven by other threads.
---MEMMGMT---
4. Reservations are released when the task completes

### `reservation_aware_resource_adaptor`

Wraps RMM device memory resource. On each allocation:
- Checks if the reservation has sufficient capacity
- If exhausted → fails gracefully, triggering `oom_reschedule_exception`
- Enables predictable memory usage per task

### Caller reservations for HOST conversions

Conversions that land data on the HOST tier draw down a caller-owned reservation instead of double-committing host capacity: the caller obtains a reservation with `make_reservation_or_null(size)` and passes it to the reservation-taking `convert_to`/`clone_to` overloads, so the converter's allocation is charged against capacity the caller already holds. If the reservation cannot be made, the call falls back — with a warning — to the `memory_space*` overload (no reservation; the converter may OOM). Call sites: `lock_or_prepare_batch` in `src/include/pipeline/batch_lock_utils.hpp` and the materialized result collector (`src/op/sirius_physical_result_collector.cpp`). The `memory_space*` overloads remain the path for GPU/DISK targets and viability probes.


### Recording

- `record(rec)` — on successful task completion
- `record_on_failure(estimated_bytes, peak)` — on OOM; keeps the **higher** peak for repeated failures with the same input size, so each retry reserves more

### Estimation

`estimate_peak_memory(estimated_bytes)` computes a weighted average of historical `peak/estimated` ratios. Records with similar estimation bases are weighted higher using a log-ratio distance function: `weight = 1 / (1 + |log(rec_est / new_est)|)`.

265:### PR reviewability
266-
267-PRs sometimes stall for weeks after a reviewer is assigned, simply because the PR wasn't actually
268-ready to review the moment CODEOWNERS pinged someone. Before marking a PR ready for review, please
269-do the following:
270-
271-1. **State the motivation, not just the mechanics.** Link the originating issue (`Closes #NNN` /
272-   `Refs #NNN`) if one exists; if there isn't one, the description itself should explain *why* the
273-   change is needed, not just summarize the diff.
274-2. **Scope the PR to one reviewable sitting.** If a reviewer can't get through it start-to-finish
275-   without losing context, either split it (see [Stacked PRs](#stacked-prs)) or explicitly justify
276-   in the description why it can't be split.
277-3. **Make the description self-sufficient.** A reviewer should be able to start reviewing without
278-   needing to ask what changed or why — cover what changed, why, how it was verified, and anything
279-   non-obvious (e.g. "intentionally doesn't handle X, tracked in #NNN").
280-4. **Open as a draft until 1-3 are actually true**, then convert to "Ready for review" — that's
281-   the point CODEOWNERS review requests and author auto-assignment (`auto-assign.yml`) trigger, so
282-   converting early means a reviewer gets pinged before there's anything reviewable yet.
283-
284-### Commit and title convention
285-
286-Sirius squash-merges PRs, the PR titles become the commit message on merge. Commits and PR titles follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format for readability.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run bench-kit TPC-H queries against the FE on 9030 with a /* marker */ so the FE audit log ties QueryId to (query, run).
# usage: run-queries.sh <tag> <tpch_data> <out_dir> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q02 ...
# writes <out_dir>/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc) and <out_dir>/<q>.r<i>.out (mysql --batch)
TAG=$1; DATA=$2; OUT=$3; TO=$4; RUNS=$5; shift 5
QD=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT; echo "query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc" > $OUT/runs.csv
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
for q in "$@"; do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  for i in $(seq 0 $RUNS); do
    phase=warm; [ $i = 0 ] && phase=cold
    start=$(date -u +%FT%T.%3N); t0=$(date +%s%N)
    if timeout $TO $M -e "/* $TAG $q r$i */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.r$i.out 2> $OUT/$q.r$i.err; then st=pass; else st=fail; rc=$?; fi
    ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000 )); rows=$(( $(wc -l < $OUT/$q.r$i.out) - 1 )); [ $rows -lt 0 ] && rows=0
    [ $st = fail ] && [ $ms -ge $((TO*1000 - 500)) ] && st=timeout
    echo "$q,$i,$phase,$st,$ms,$rows,$start" >> $OUT/runs.csv
    echo "$q r$i $phase $st ${ms}ms rows=$rows $( [ $st != pass ] && head -c 160 $OUT/$q.r$i.err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ $st != pass ] && break   # a failing run skips the rest of that query (bench.sh semantics)
  done
done

# Fix 1 spec: fail the query fast when an OOM retry cannot make progress

Implementation spec for an engineer working alone in the worktree
`/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-oom-failfast` (branch off `perf/profile-sf1000` =
`45dab3be`, GPU 0 assigned). Source anchors below are `file:line` in that tree; the engine files this
fix touches are byte-identical on `origin/dev` (checked with `git diff --stat origin/dev..d24f02c4`
over the touched files: only `task_scheduler.{hpp,cpp}` differ, +53 lines that do not overlap the
edits here), so the same line numbers hold for the upstream PR. Evidence bundle:
`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/` (cited as `E/...`). "Measured" means read from a named file or produced by
re-running `E/agent-notes/skeptic-oom4/retry_stats.py` today; "inference" is marked.

## 0. What was decided and why

Two judges scored the three designs (surgical / robust / upstream). Their totals tie: surgical 43,
upstream 43, robust 32. Both rejected robust's config schema, constructor-signature churn and
exception-type change; both asked for the same set of merges. This spec is the merge:

| piece | taken from | why |
|---|---|---|
| Decision made in the **reschedule path**, confirmed by the retry's own OOM | upstream | The gate-time abort (surgical) would fire ~40 ms earlier at best: both fire at the first retry-1 gate/OOM (section 3.6). Confirming by an actual OOM removes the pre-emptive-abort risk at negligible cost, and the reschedule path already has the error-exit shape and the operator name. |
| Hard lower bound `live + requested` recorded by the OOM handler | surgical | It is exact (raa accounting, section 2.3) and replaces upstream's `granted < floor` test, which judge 2 showed degenerates (the floor is raised to >= 2 x granted before the throw, so it is always true). |
| Pure, header-only predicate with a GPU-free Catch2 table | upstream | Reviewable decision rule; CI-testable without a GPU. |
| Scheduler-wide progress signals: `completed_epoch` + `inflight_first_attempts` in a small struct owned by `task_scheduler`, passed to executors through a **defaulted** extra ctor argument | robust (via judge 1) | Closes the multi-GPU blind spot (a completion on another GPU can make a subscribed GPU-0 batch convertible, `downgrade_executor.cpp:231-232`). No config, no signature break: the single test construction site keeps compiling. |
| `has_error()` early-out before the gate blocks | robust | Stops a failed query's queued retries from each costing the manager a blocking `make_reservation`. |
| `oom_reschedules` / `futile_aborts` counters in `executor_metrics` | robust | Makes component-test assertions exact. |
| Holder-task test that pins cucascade's IDLE semantics; arm-B log assertions; "held outside any task reservation" wording | surgical | The proof depends on partial grants being issued only when no reservation is alive; this test fails loudly if cucascade changes. |
| `has_disk_tier()` in the message; stale-doc fix at `execution-flow.md:150` | upstream | Gives the documented-but-uncalled hook (`downgrade_executor.hpp:155-161`) its caller. |
| `MAX_RETRIES = 100` and the 50 ms backoff unchanged; constant hoisted to file scope so both messages name it | all three | The #732 cross-GPU contention budget is not this fix's business. |
| Hysteresis = 1 (abort at the first retry whose OOM confirms the gate's verdict) | surgical / judge 2 | The bound is hard; N=2 (robust) costs a full extra round (2.4 s for q08/q09) for no safety. |
| Acceptance measured **from the first OOM in the engine log**, not from client start | all three | q18's first OOM is at +9.29 s because its own senders run first; q08/q09 rounds are 2.3-2.4 s. |

Dropped: robust's YAML knob, `gpu_pipeline_executor_config`, `oom_details` on the exception, HOST-tier
claims (`task_scheduler.cpp:91-93` builds GPU-tier executors only); surgical's gate-time `break`;
upstream's per-executor `_tasks_executed` mark and creation-time snapshot (replaced by the shared
epoch snapshotted at the gate, which also avoids the one-round delay the single stray completion per
window could otherwise cause).

## 1. Goal and non-goals

**Goal.** A GPU pipeline task whose OOM retry provably cannot be granted what its last OOM needed fails
the query at that retry instead of replaying the same OOM up to 100 times, and the error names the
cause: bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any task reservation vs the pool, bytes the
downgrade freed, disk-tier state, and that nothing completed or was running that could release memory.

Measured target (1 CN, 100 GiB pool, SF1000): q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 currently die after 101.5 /
168.3 / 232.5 / 103.9 / 54.2 / 114.5 s (`E/cn1/runs/runs.csv`), 774.9 s of the 910.3 s sweep, with
17,900 reschedule warnings and 17,917 "0 bytes freed ... proceeding with partial reservation" lines.
After this fix each dies within one retry round of its first OOM (section 6).

**Non-goals.**
- Making the six queries pass on 1 CN (fix 4), attributing the held bytes to fragments or dropping a
  dead query's parked output (fix 2), FE cardinalities (fix 3).
- Changing `MAX_RETRIES`, the backoff, the retry-floor policy (`2 x reservation`), the downgrade
  executor's misleading "disk not configured" WARN (`downgrade_executor.cpp:357-363`, belongs to 4b),
  the watchdog fingerprint, or the sink-deferral OOM path (`gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:721-751`; see
  decision 3).
- Any CN (`experimental/starrocks`), FE, proto, cucascade or configuration change. The error string
  already travels verbatim to the client (section 3.5).

## 2. The measured failure and the three facts the fix rests on

### 2.1 The loop (measured)

`src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348` `static constexpr uint32_t MAX_RETRIES = 100;`, `:409`

reservation gate proceeds on a partial grant after the downgrade freed nothing (`:262-271`, the WARN
"after downgrade ({} bytes freed), reservation still partial ({}/{} bytes) ... proceeding with partial
reservation"). Per query on cn1 (`retry_stats.py`, re-run 2026-09-03):

| q05 | 25 | 2500 | +1.61 s | +1.61..+2.62 (1.01 s) | 101.5 s |

Every original reaches exactly retry 100; every OOM is `GPU_SCAN` index 0 with
`global usage 107374182400` (the limit); every one of the 17,917 gate passes freed 0 and granted
partially; zero reschedule lines fall outside the six windows on cn1, and none exist on the three
other CNs of the 4-CN sweep. The q05 chain of original task 2567 (`E/cn1/engine-cn0.log:49219-49223`,
`:61597`, `:61723`): first attempt granted 3,318,948,864 of 5,803,790,251 requested, OOM asking
748,875,880 B at peak 3,376,381,184 B; every retry granted 3,076,488,960 of the 6,637,897,728 floor,
freed 0, same OOM; `exceeded 100 retries` at 13:05:24.553, drain done at .624 (71 ms), CN "fragment
run failed" 74 ms later (`E/cn1/cluster.log`).

Rounds are lockstep because the pool is full: the manager thread blocks in `make_reservation` until
the one running task releases (Quent q05 fragment 5774: `Rsv=99.940 s` of a 101.2 s window,
`E/cn1-quent.txt`). At most one task executes on the GPU at a time during the storm (fact A).

### 2.2 Fact A: a partial grant means no other reservation is alive on the space

`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`: `make_reservation` loops on `make_reservation_or_null`
and only returns `make_reservation_upto(size)` when `_notification_channel->wait()` returns `IDLE`.
`cucascade/src/memory/notification_channel.cpp:49-60`: `IDLE` is returned only when
`_n_active_notifiers == 0`. Every reservation owns a notifier for its lifetime
(`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381`, `memory_reservation.hpp:183-198`). The upto grant is
`min(request, reservation_limit - total_allocated)` (`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:375-380`
-> `do_reserve_upto` `:535-543` -> `add_bounded` `cucascade/include/cucascade/utils/atomics.hpp:87-97`).
So for a **partial** grant, `reservation_limit - granted == total_allocated at the gate == bytes held
outside any reservation` (parked fragment output, pinned tables, idle batches). Exact, independent of
`reservation_limit_fraction`; on the CN the fraction is 1.0 (`engine_settings.rs:98,102`).

### 2.3 Fact B: a LIMIT_EXCEEDED OOM proves `live + requested > reservation`

`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:184-214` (`check_reservation_and_handle_overflow`): an
allocation charges the pool only for the part of `live + requested` that exceeds the stream's
reservation (`upstream_tracking_size == 0` while `post_allocation_inc < reservation_size`). The pool
check `_total_allocated_bytes.try_add(tracking_bytes, _capacity)` (`:465`) throws
`cucascade_out_of_memory(..., LIMIT_EXCEEDED, allocation_bytes, ...)` (`:477-482`). Hence a
LIMIT_EXCEEDED OOM implies `live + requested > reservation` strictly. `gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:433-457`
already computes both (`cc_oom->requested_bytes`, `_allocator->get_allocated_bytes(stream)`) and folds
them into the floor (`gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-108`); the per-stream peak is updated with the failed
allocation included (`:199`), which is why the logged `peak allocated 3376381184` equals
`live + requested` for q05 (inference from the code path; the log prints peak, not live).

Combining A and B for a retry at gate k with a partial IDLE grant and 0 bytes freed:
`granted_k = limit - held_k <= limit - held_{k-1}` (held only grows during a fragment run; the CN
releases parked output only after the fragment finishes, `engine.rs:278-280`, finding B1) and the
previous OOM proved the task needs `> reservation_{k-1} >= granted_k`. The retry will OOM again, and so
will every later one unless something outside this task frees memory: a downgrade (shows as
`freed > 0`), or a task completing (shows in the shared epoch / in-flight counter).

### 2.4 Fact C: `freed == 0` is the only trustworthy "nothing convertible" signal

`request_downgrade(...).get()` returns the bytes freed by TIER 1 (repositories,
`downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`) and TIER 2 (queued tasks, `:294-300`), `set_value(total_bytes)`
at `:397`. Parked sink output escapes TIER 1 by design (`streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, finding
B2). `has_viable_downgrade_target()` (`downgrade_executor.cpp:406-446`) probes HOST capacity, not
candidate existence, and is true in the SF1000 case (160 GiB HOST, empty). Use `freed`.

## 3. Mechanism

### 3.1 New header `src/include/pipeline/retry_futility.hpp` (GPU-free, header-only)

Includes only `<atomic> <cstddef> <cstdint> <format> <optional> <string>`. No CUDA, no cucascade.

```cpp
namespace sirius::pipeline {

/// Context-wide progress signals consulted by the OOM fail-fast. One instance per task_scheduler,
/// shared by every gpu_pipeline_executor it owns; relaxed/acquire atomics, no locks.
struct execution_progress {
  std::atomic<std::uint64_t> completed_epoch{0};         ///< +1 per task whose execute() returned normally, any executor
  std::atomic<std::int64_t>  inflight_first_attempts{0}; ///< first-attempt tasks (retry_count == 0) currently inside execute(), any executor
};

/// What the GPU executor's reservation gate saw for one attempt. Written by the manager thread
/// right before set_reservation(); read by the reschedule path after the attempt threw.
struct retry_gate_observation {
  std::size_t   requested_bytes         = 0;     ///< bytes_needs after the space-max clamp
  std::size_t   granted_bytes           = 0;     ///< reservation->size() handed to the task
  std::size_t   freed_by_downgrade      = 0;     ///< bytes the gate's downgrade request freed (0 when none ran)
  bool          downgrade_requested     = false; ///< the gate asked a downgrade executor (partial grant + executor present)
  bool          disk_tier_configured    = false; ///< downgrade_executor::has_disk_tier()
  std::size_t   space_max_bytes         = 0;     ///< memory_space::get_max_memory() (the reservation limit)
  std::uint64_t completed_epoch_at_gate = 0;     ///< execution_progress::completed_epoch read before make_reservation()
};

struct retry_futility_input {
  bool          is_oom                      = false; ///< the exception is an oom_reschedule_exception
  std::uint32_t retry_count                 = 0;     ///< of the task that just threw (0 = first attempt)
  std::size_t   oom_required_bytes          = 0;     ///< live + requested recorded by the OOM handler; 0 = unknown
  std::optional<retry_gate_observation> gate;        ///< this attempt's gate observation
  std::uint64_t completed_epoch_now         = 0;
  std::int64_t  inflight_first_attempts_now = 0;
};

/// Returns std::nullopt when another retry may succeed; otherwise the human-readable reason it
/// cannot (used verbatim in the query error). Pure: no I/O, no globals.
inline std::optional<std::string> assess_retry_futility(const retry_futility_input& in);

}  // namespace sirius::pipeline
```

Decision rule, in this order (each early-return is one row of the test table in 4.1):

1. `!in.is_oom` -> nullopt (CUDA-launch reschedules keep the plain 100-retry budget).
2. `in.retry_count == 0` -> nullopt (a first attempt never fails fast; partial first attempts often succeed).
3. `!in.gate` -> nullopt (defensive: the gate did not record).
4. `gate.granted_bytes >= gate.requested_bytes` -> nullopt (full grant: the gate was not the constraint; this is
   the #732 contention shape and the existing `xl_task` test).
5. `gate.freed_by_downgrade != 0` -> nullopt (spilling is making progress; fix 4b lives here).
6. `in.oom_required_bytes == 0 || in.oom_required_bytes <= gate.granted_bytes` -> nullopt (unknown need, or it would fit).
7. `in.completed_epoch_now != gate.completed_epoch_at_gate` -> nullopt (something finished since the gate; its
   memory may now be convertible or free).
8. `in.inflight_first_attempts_now != 0` -> nullopt (a first attempt is running somewhere and may release memory).
9. Otherwise futile. Reason text (q05 numbers, `held = space_max - granted`):

```
the last attempt needed at least 3376381184 bytes (3.14 GiB) on its own stream but the reservation gate could
grant only 3076488960 bytes (2.87 GiB) of the 6637897728 requested; 104297693440 bytes (97.1% of the
107374182400-byte space) are held outside any task reservation and were not convertible by the downgrade
executor, which freed 0 bytes (disk tier not configured); no task completed and no first attempt was running
since this attempt's reservation was granted, so another retry would hit the same limit (retry cap 100)
```
When `downgrade_requested == false` the middle clause reads "and no downgrade executor is attached to this
memory space". The GiB figures are `bytes / 1073741824.0` with `{:.2f}`; percentages `{:.1f}`. The substrings
`held outside any task reservation` and `freed 0 bytes` are contract (tests and acceptance grep them).

**first statement of the lambda** an RAII guard:
```cpp
struct first_attempt_guard {   // file-scope helper in the anonymous namespace
  execution_progress* p;
  explicit first_attempt_guard(execution_progress* progress) : p(progress) { if (p) p->inflight_first_attempts.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel); }
  ~first_attempt_guard() { if (p) p->inflight_first_attempts.fetch_sub(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel); }
  first_attempt_guard(const first_attempt_guard&) = delete; first_attempt_guard& operator=(const first_attempt_guard&) = delete;
};
// inside the lambda, first line:
first_attempt_guard inflight(first_attempt ? _progress.get() : nullptr);
```
Every exit of the lambda (normal, `return` in the reschedule catch, `return` in the generic catches) runs the
destructor, so the counter cannot leak. The uncounted window between `dispatch()` and the lambda's first
statement is harmless: a task that has not started holds no memory that a retry's next gate could reclaim.

**Success path** (`:309-310`): after `_tasks_executed.fetch_add(1, ...)` add
`_progress->completed_epoch.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_acq_rel);`.

    _futile_aborts.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    auto message = std::format(
      "GPU pipeline task gave up after {} OOM {} with no way to make progress for original task {} on GPU:{}: {}; {}",

      _memory_space->get_device_id(), ex.what(), *reason);

input.summary: The two judges tied (surgical 43, upstream 43, robust 32) and asked for the same merges, so the spec is that merge: the decision is made in the executor's reschedule path (upstream's shape, confirmed by the retry's own OOM, same exit as the MAX_RETRIES path) using surgical's hard lower bound `live + requested` recorded by the OOM handler (replacing upstream's `granted < floor` test, which judge 2 showed is always true because the floor is raised to >= 2x granted before the throw), a pure header-only predicate with a GPU-free Catch2 table, and robust's scheduler-wide progress signals (`completed_epoch` + `inflight_first_attempts` in a small struct owned by task_scheduler, passed through a defaulted extra ctor argument so the one test construction site keeps compiling) plus its `has_error()` early-out at the gate and `oom_reschedules`/`futile_aborts` metrics. Rule: OOM exception, retry_count >= 1, gate granted less than requested (partial grant, which cucascade issues only when no other reservation is alive: memory_space.cpp:257-266, notification_channel.cpp:49-60), downgrade freed 0, OOM-recorded need > grant, epoch unchanged since the gate, no first attempt in flight anywhere. MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff are untouched (hoisted to file scope); no config, CN, FE, proto or cucascade change; the error text travels verbatim to the client through the verified existing path and names bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any task reservation vs the pool (exact under IDLE: limit - grant), bytes freed, disk-tier state. Predicted SF1000 effect (inference from the measured chain, re-run of retry_stats.py today): each of q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 fails one retry round after its first OOM (client ~2.9/4.3/4.9/2.6/10.2/4.0 s vs 101.5/168.3/232.5/103.9/54.2/114.5 s today); the 15 passing queries never enter the changed branch (0 reschedule lines in their windows on cn1 and cn4). Touched engine files are byte-identical between origin/dev and the perf base (only task_scheduler.{hpp,cpp} differ by +53 non-overlapping lines), so the PR can target dev self-contained.
